sections.title: Driver task management menu
sections.content:
![](/uploads/d0fbe814f42f95f38a97cfa5.png)

**The task management menus are:**

1. Dispatcher tasks: contains the list of tasks for dispatchers.

sections.title: Creating a task
sections.content:
## The system separates tasks into two kinds - Tasks tied to a customer's container or waybill: - These are the tasks that get the waybill done, for example: pick up empty container, drop off empty container, pick up laden container, deliver laden container. - They have to be created from the container or waybill screen. - They also affect the driver's salary, because driver salary is calculated per waybill. - Tasks not tied to a customer's container or waybill: - These tasks do not belong to any container or waybill. The system still lets you assign a trailer and create a dispatch order for them so a driver can carry them out as usual. - Whether dispatchers use this depends on how they work. ## Creating a task for a container or waybill - Step 1: open a container or waybill → go to the [Tasks] tab. ![](/uploads/86e62ba822b465bcbd263ac9.png) - Step 2: click **Add a line** to create a task for that container or waybill. The system shows a popup for the task details; fill in the **Task information** section as shown below. ![](/uploads/037bd24ca66d84807c3cb3a6.png) | **Field** | **Description** | |:-----------|:----------| | Task | Select a task type, for example "Pick up empty container". | | Location | Select where the task is carried out. | | Contact | Enter the contact at that location, if any. | | Mobile | Enter the contact's phone number. | | Note for the driver | A note for the driver, if any. It is shown in the mobile app. | | Planned date | Enter the date you plan the driver to carry out the task. The dispatcher sets a date that makes dispatching work well. | | Deadline | Enter the deadline from the paperwork, or one the dispatcher sets to keep track of the task. | | Plan | The container plan at the customer's warehouse. Applies to tasks such as "Deliver laden container" or "Drop off empty container" at a customer warehouse.

The values are: drop container, detach trailer, store vehicle. This is also shown in the mobile app so the driver knows the plan. | - Step 3: click **SAVE & CLOSE** if you only want one task, or **SAVE & NEW** to create another one. The task you added appears as below; you can reorder it so the sequence is right. ![](/uploads/c106f072776fc6c92f596db1.png) - Step 4: click **SAVE** on the container or waybill, or press **CTRL + S**, to save. ![](/uploads/96702d4c259c1653bf3aba08.png) Once that is done the system generates a task code, as below: ![](/uploads/b6636671664057525bce798f.png) ## Creating a task not tied to a container or waybill - Step 1: go to one of the driver task management menus → click **NEW** to create a task. ![](/uploads/28b7d7a81fbfd4ad536926ca.png) - Step 2: enter the task details, the same way as for a waybill task, and click SAVE to finish. ![](/uploads/ba1987b67d71586aa138359b.png)

sections.title: Starting a task
sections.content:
The system lets a dispatcher start a task. This is useful in a few situations:

- **Doing it on the driver's behalf:** normally the driver starts the task in the mobile app. But sometimes the driver cannot use the app — for example they have lost their phone — and then the dispatcher can start the task for them.

- **Orders handed to a cooperative or an outside carrier:** here the dispatcher keeps track of progress by phone or another channel and starts the task in the system.

## Steps

### Step 1

Open the task you want to start, either from a task management menu or from a dispatch order (1) → then click **START** (2).

![](/uploads/4a649f2373369d3954d82bd5.png)

### Step 2

The system asks whether you are sure you want to start the task. If you are, click OK.

![](/uploads/70741bdafdd69a5f0535cc26.png)

### Step 3

The system shows a popup. Enter the actual start time — it defaults to now — and click **OK**.

![](/uploads/16e75aaa2529decd960aee93.png)

## Result

The system moves the task to the **IN PROGRESS** state.

![](/uploads/3ccb6fe384deaa8ccf0ededa.png)

sections.title: Completing a task
sections.content:
The system lets a dispatcher complete a task. This is useful in a few situations:

- **Doing it on the driver's behalf:** normally the driver completes the task in the mobile app. But sometimes the driver cannot use the app — for example they have lost their phone — and then the dispatcher can complete the task for them.

- **Orders handed to a cooperative or an outside carrier:** here the dispatcher keeps track of progress by phone or another channel and completes the task in the system.

## Steps

### Step 1

Open the task you want to complete, either from a task management menu or by clicking the task on a dispatch order (1) → attach the related images and documents (2) on the task's [Documents] tab.

![](/uploads/69612f249a98a76b5c568e67.png)

### Step 2

→ Then click **COMPLETE**.

![](/uploads/0e0c2eb12e868a50e715a32d.png)

### Step 3

The system asks whether you are sure you want to complete the task. If you are, click OK.

![](/uploads/3c5aa02cdab6bf942435fc2c.png)

### Step 4

The system shows a popup. Enter the actual completion time, and the container and seal numbers for the "pick up empty container" task of an export full container waybill, then click **OK**.

![](/uploads/a2dc0c0352d2a50d2a45fa10.png)

Result: the system moves the task to the **COMPLETED** state:

![](/uploads/bbd8c5f49ed707c7dac29a1f.png)

sections.title: Reverting a task to not started
sections.content:
## Note

The system lets you revert a task to the not started state when it is In progress, Completed or Cancelled.

## Reverting a task to not started

### Step 1

Open the task you want to revert → click **REVERT TO NOT STARTED**.

![](/uploads/388a1713e8c1d40cbb2e652c.png)

### Step 2

The system asks you to confirm. If you are sure, click OK.

![](/uploads/61ec4948e28668009f4bf3b2.png)

The system moves the task back to the **NOT STARTED** state:

![](/uploads/b44a23fb3b0b782c2e1f89f2.png)

sections.title: Canceling a task
sections.content:
## Note

The system lets you cancel a task, but only while it is **NOT STARTED**.

If you cancel every task of a container or waybill, that container or waybill also moves to the **CANCELED** state automatically.

## Canceling a task

### Step 1

Open the task you want to cancel → then click **CANCEL**.

![](/uploads/72f2ab5d0d3fbcc456ca45e3.png)

### Step 2

The system asks you to confirm. If you are sure, click OK.

![](/uploads/da073783ff4ef1e2125bf0f1.png)

The system moves the task to the **CANCELED** state:

![](/uploads/8f06d33b0da6c8b78f1df1c5.png)

sections.title: Deleting a task
sections.content:
## Note

The system lets you delete a task, but only while it is **NOT STARTED or CANCELED** and the container or waybill has not been confirmed. Once the container or waybill is confirmed, you can only cancel the task.

## Deleting a task

- **Step 1:** open a container or waybill → scroll down to the task list → select the task you want to delete (1) → click "Delete task" (2) → confirm in the popup.

![](/uploads/7803ec4d58e2504f2e840795.png)

![](/uploads/5b7ea41865b022db305ae49b.png)

- **Step 2**: open the task list in one of the task menus → tick the tasks you want to delete → click ACTIONS → click the delete action.

![](/uploads/cfc6ea5cf7f44233dbd61e31.png)

- **Step 3:** the system asks you to confirm. If you are sure, click DELETE.

![](/uploads/4a9743e1197af07e21990baf.png)

sections.title: The overdue status of a task
sections.content:
## The overdue status has three values

1. Overdue: past the deadline.

2. Due soon: within 6 hours of the deadline.

3. Normal: more than 6 hours before the deadline.

## In the task list

The system shows a light column so you can tell the overdue status at a glance.

- Overdue: red light

- Due soon: yellow light

- Normal: green light

![](/uploads/78325bbe2c2060534b8c48b4.png)

## On the details screen of a task

When a task is "Due soon" or "Overdue", the system shows a matching ribbon as below.

![](/uploads/4a27b57cc7ce05735bd7b611.png)

The system also provides the "Overdue" and "Due soon" filters and a grouping by "Overdue status" so you can filter the data easily:

![](/uploads/b742f6aa1a2c605101b3d379.png)

![](/uploads/8fe346462cd917a2e42dce68.png)
